physicalNotes: Radius 0.17869569 Jupiter radii from Wells et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.487.1865W), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.487.1865W/abstract): 12,775.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0147 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 11.0248821 d
sources.shape: Wells et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.487.1865W), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname WELLS_ET_AL__2019): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.07487 au and stellar radius 0.455 solar radii; Wells et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.487.1865W), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname WELLS_ET_AL__2019): inclination 89.4 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460251.64402 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 9 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
